compaction.//: JSON takes no comments, so the reasoning lives in these keys. Context window is 65536 (pi/models.json).
compaction.//summariser: The summary's CONTENT is not configurable from here. pi 0.85.1 reads exactly three keys under `compaction` - enabled, reserveTokens, keepRecentTokens (dist/core/settings-manager.js getCompactionSettings, CompactionSettings in its .d.ts) - and nothing else. The prompt that writes the summary is the const UPDATE_SUMMARIZATION_PROMPT in dist/core/compaction/compaction.js, and its `customInstructions` hook is reachable only from `/compact <text>` typed by hand or from the programmatic API; the auto-compaction path passes undefined. That prompt says 'PRESERVE all existing information from the previous summary', which is why a summary never corrects a coordinate it carried before. The one real lever is a `session_before_compact` extension in pi/extensions/ or ~/.pi/agent/extensions/, which can supply customInstructions or the whole summary. Not taken: the fact that its own memory goes stale now lives in games/openrct2/prompt.md instead, where it costs no extension to maintain. Do not add a key here expecting it to bite - pi's loader ignores unknown keys silently.
compaction.//trigger: WHAT PI COMPARES AGAINST reserveTokens, because this file used to say something else and the something else was wrong. pi 0.85.1 does NOT size the context at chars/4 when it decides to compact. agent-session.js `_checkCompaction` uses `calculateContextTokens(assistantMessage.usage)` - the provider's own totalTokens, prompt plus completion - and `_compactBeforeNextAssistantResponse` uses `estimateContextTokens(messages)`, which is that same last usage figure plus a chars/4 estimate of ONLY the messages appended since it. The trigger is therefore in real tokens as counted by whatever server answered, and it needs no correction for a model whose tokenizer is denser than Qwen's. The recorded runs prove it. pi/sessions holds 12 compactions and every one fired within 1637 tokens of the threshold then in force: four at tokensBefore 49458-50067 against the 49152 that pi's own default reserve of 16384 gave before this block existed, and six at 53299-54885 against the 53248 that reserveTokens 12288 gave after it. A chars/4 trigger could not have fired at all - the largest chars/4 estimate of any recorded conversation is 28634. The old claim that the real context at the trigger was ~75k on a 65536 window was wrong by that same factor: the largest real prompt sent across 19 sessions is 53896 tokens, and with maxTokens 8192 on top the largest request was 62088, inside a genuine 64k window rather than over it. No recorded run would have been rejected by a hosted 64k model. chars/4 still costs real tokens in exactly two places, and both are priced below.
compaction.//reserveTokens:
14336, and it is not a round number for its own sake. It is maxTokens, plus what the pre-request gate undercounts, plus stated headroom.
   65536   W, the window these settings are computed against (pi/models.json contextWindow). Deliberately the smallest genuine hosted window this repo intends to run, NOT oMLX's max_model_len of 262144: a run has to behave the same locally and on OpenRouter, and a local run that never compacts would be scored on a different axis from a hosted one that does.
    8192   M, maxTokens. The model's next response shares the window with its prompt, so the reserve can never be smaller than this. The largest response that completed is 5697 tokens; two recorded runs hit the 8192 cap outright.
    2052   D, the one place chars/4 still costs real tokens. `_compactBeforeNextAssistantResponse` adds ceil(chars/4) for every message appended since the last usage report, and these payloads run at 2.77 chars/token (measured over the 50 recorded trailing blocks of 4000+ chars: 138k chars against 49.8k real tokens). So C chars of trailing tool output are undercounted by C/2.77 - C/4 = C/9. The largest single tool result in pi/sessions is 18494 chars (find_build_sites, since replaced): pi counts it as 4624 and it really costs 6676.
    4092   H, headroom, 6.2% of the window.
   -----
   14336   reserveTokens.
So compaction fires above W - R = 51200 real tokens, and the worst request that can still be sent is 51200 + D + M = 61444, which is 4092 below 65536.
THE INVARIANT, which is what to keep if any of these move: reserveTokens >= maxTokens + (largest trailing block in chars) / 9. At 14336 that tolerates a 55296-char trailing block, three times the largest ever recorded. Change maxTokens in pi/models.json and this number has to change with it.
Do not go below 10240 whatever else happens: the summariser's own output cap is min(floor(0.8 * reserveTokens), model.maxTokens), which is 8192 here and starts shrinking below 10240.
compaction.//keepRecentTokens: The retained tail after a compaction, and the one number here that pi really does measure at chars/4: findCutPoint walks back through the entries summing estimateTokens (chars/4) until it has keepRecentTokens. These payloads run at 2.68 chars/token across all 548 recorded turn transitions (788k chars against 294k real tokens), so the real tail is about 1.49x this number: 10000 retains ~14900 real tokens, where 20000 retained ~29800. This is the one lever that can cost play quality - below it the model leans on a prose summary carrying no coordinates - so it was halved rather than taken to the 8000 that was modelled. It fits inside the new trigger: after a compaction the context is the fixed floor (~11900 real tokens of system prompt, tool schemas and first user message), plus a summary (median 2200 output tokens over the 12 recorded compactions), plus that ~14900 tail - about 29000 of the 51200 trigger, leaving roughly 22 turns before the next one at the measured 1020 real tokens a turn.
compaction.//whenItFires: What this costs in run comparability, recorded because it is a benchmark property rather than a performance one. A compacted run is scored on play skill, self-summarisation and error propagation; an uncompacted one on play skill alone. Replaying the 19 recorded sessions against each threshold, with the compactions that actually happened undone so the curve is not truncated: at reserveTokens 12288 seven runs cross, first crossing at turns 23-44 (median 33); at 14336 the same seven cross, at turns 23-43 (median 31); at 16384 still the same seven, median 28. So this change moves the first compaction about two turns earlier and moves no run across the line. What decides whether a run compacts at all is its length - the seven that cross are the long ones - so the axis a run is scored on is still chosen by how verbose the model was that day. Fixing that is not a reserveTokens change and is not attempted here.
